---
title: Course Description
subtitle: 'All Data Are Local: Introduction to Data Literacy'
---

This course introduces data literacy for Data Design + Art. It starts from a simple idea: data are not given. People make data through observation, selection, classification, measurement, storage, and design.

The main text is Yanni Alexander Loukissas's _All Data Are Local_ [-@loukissas2019]. We use the Introduction and Chapters 1 and 2 on Day 1. We use Chapters 6 and 7 on Day 2. The course asks three questions throughout:

- What do we gain when we turn the world into data?
- What do we lose?
- Who makes these decisions?

Between the two course days, students study selected sections of _Introduction to Modern Statistics (2e)_ [-@cetinkayarundel2024ims]. These sections provide basic statistical language for observations, variables, samples, distributions, and common charts. Day 2 starts with a short multiple-choice quiz on this material.

Students also bring their own dataset. They use it to connect statistical description with critical data practice.

## Learning outcomes

After the course, students can:

- distinguish a **dataset** from its **data setting**;
- explain how observations and categories become data;
- identify the origin, purpose, limits, and missing context of a dataset;
- use basic statistical terms to describe a dataset;
- explain how place, institutions, tools, and interfaces shape data;
- describe a dataset in a clear, critical, and responsible way.
